implementation: One32-thread wave owns a16x16 QK tile. The original matrix result lanes retain eight sequential canonical carries, eliminating shared approximate/residue output redistribution to other waves. Private-key and shared-key versions both use coalesced shared query copies. The original116-byte rows, headroom5 core, integer recovery, loss/exception compensation, fallback, modulo sign disambiguation and every K16 normalization are unchanged. The preceding64-column cooperative byte-residue kernel and selected prepared QK are concurrent controls.
correctness_scope: The recovery lemma still requires absolute native error below128; bounded integer arithmetic does not prove that hardware condition. The referenced preceding native integer checks observe maximum error28 with no recovery failures; their unchanged implementation hashes are checked. This run does not repeat that independent core fixture. All generated/captured QK score bits compare to original complete canonical GPU scores plus independent CPU dot checks. The original immutable capture provenance and comparable golden component are attached; no new GB10 model request or token-loop result is created. The q8192 component repeats1023 original rows. Counts across variants and attempts include repeated input identities and masked score slots. Every warmup and measured output, prepared input encoding, original operand, guard and unused score tail is checked. Reference outputs are comparison data only.
timing_scope: Full QK includes canonical carries and exceptions, query encoding in every slab timer and one key encoding. The selected prepared control includes Q/K preparation. Full variants rotate across slabs and each receives one warmup plus three completed measurements. Allocation, reset and validation are outside component clocks; all bounded process walls and source/binary identities are attached. No probability, PV, model load, TTFT or token generation is measured.

decision.decision: Keep both single-wave layouts isolated. Every generated and captured score bit passes, but private/shared-key complete QK costs1012.1615/1167.6111ms at the repeated-row q8192 component versus350.2608ms for selected prepared QK and848.2599ms for the preceding cooperative64-column byte-residue control. Eliminating shared product redistribution does not overcome the larger per-wave work and operand access costs in these measurements. No production integration is justified; continue structural producer/consumer work.
